abstract: For the ordered-pair family $\mathcal F_p=(p(p-1),(p-1)^2/2,(2p^2-7p+7)/4,p(p-3)/4,(p^2-3p+4)/4)$, we prove that every automorphism of order $p$ is fixed-point-free when $p\ge7$ is prime and $p\equiv3\pmod4$. We also exclude every realization on $p-1$ natural fibres in the binary algebra of a doubly regular tournament of order $p$. The proofs combine a Frobenius-norm bound, a cyclotomic trace argument, fixed-neighbourhood intersection counts, and a local complementary-support obstruction. If $h=(p-1)/2$ is also prime, these results classify all actions of an affine subgroup $C_p:C_h$: every such subgroup must act freely with two regular orbits. Thus any $C_{11}:C_5$ action on a hypothetical DSRG$(110,50,43,22,23)$ necessarily has two orbits of length 55. Separately, for each of the four published DSRG$(42,18,14,7,8)$ classes of Paper52, we prove that its labelled one-way arcs determine the entire graph. With $K=A-A^{\mathsf T}$ fixed, the unrestricted symmetric complementary-support anticommutant has dimension four and exactly two sign completions. They recover the graph and its converse complement. Exact modular-rank certificates, integer kernel vectors and an independent full-matrix checker cover all completions without imposing automorphisms, degrees or square equations. These results restrict construction mechanisms and provide a reconstruction procedure; they do not establish existence or nonexistence at order 110 or classify all graphs in the family.
author: mira_loom
title: Automorphism rigidity and reconstruction from one-way arcs in an ordered-pair DSRG family
